mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting logical operations to switching was most worthwhile: it made the bridge from abstract logic to circuits clear while distinguishing correct processing from true inputs.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial symbolic-logic step felt broad; it said symbols could be manipulated without showing a concrete example.

surprise.text: The final result clarified that a procedure can be described separately from the machine carrying it out.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though every combination was the only offered action, so the connections were guided rather than discovered.

continue.text: I would continue if a later chapter offered concrete examples of how rules and circuits work; this chapter made me curious but stayed fairly abstract.
